rules.text:
The address for service of an individual who is not represented by a lawyer of record and is not required to be served in accordance with rule 12.55 is the most recent of [Service of documents]
(a) an address provided to the Court and all other parties by the individual in writing, (b) an address provided on the record during a Court appearance, and (c) the address provided in the most recently filed document in the proceeding.

commentary.text:
Rule 12.59 places time constraints on a party’s ability to appeal any aspect of a divorce judgment including child and spousal support,168although the 30-day time limit is a normal appeal period with the Rules. Walter v. Siler, [2017] A.J. No. 1425, 2017 ABQB 810 at para. 26 (Alta. Q.B.). The Court of Appeal may extend the deadline to file a notice of appeal beyond 30 days after the date an order in the divorce proceeding is made if the applicant satisfies all elements of the test set out in Cairns v.
Cairns: Caldwell v. Caldwell Cairns , [2013] A.J. No. 287, 2013 ABCA 126 at paras. 7-11 (Alta. C.A.); v. Cairns, [1931] A.J. No. 76, 26 Alta LR 69 (Alta. C.A.).
• that the applicant had a intention to appeal and that there were special bona fide circumstances which excused or justified the failure to file the notice of appeal on time;
• that the respondent would not be so seriously prejudiced as to make it unjust.
The prejudice to the respondent must be specific; mere extension of the litigation is not enough;
• that the applicant has not taken already the benefits of the judgment from which she or he is seeking to appeal; and • that the applicant’s proposed appeal has a reasonable chance of success.
The court retains an overriding discretion to extend the time to appeal even if an applicant has not met all branches of the test, although it is more likely that an extension will Cairns be granted where each element is satisfied. Balisky v. Balisky Andres v. Andres , [2019] A.J. No. 1424, 2019 ABCA 404 (Alta. C.A.); , [2023] A.J. No. 120, 2023 ABCA 42 (Alta. C.A.).

commentary.text:
Appeals from the Court of King’s Bench sitting as the original court hearing the matter are appeals as of right.An appeal is the proper mechanism Family Law Act to vary a rule 12.51 final order made in chambers. Panasiuk v. Leclercq, [2015] A.J. No. 811, 2015 ABQB 464 at para. 33 (Alta. Q.B.). With the repeal of rule 12.60(2), the process and time limits for appealing a decision of the Court of King’s Bench sitting as the original court is now wholly governed by the standard rules for appealing King’s Bench decisions found in Part 14.
Time Limits – Pursuant to rule 14.8 the deadline for filing a notice of appeal is one month after the “date of decision”, not when the order is filed — older cases should be read with caution. See , [2013] A.J. No. 102, 2013 ABCA 55 at paras. 5-7 (Alta. C.A.); Johnson v. Jordan Beck v. Ackmann, [2013] A.J. No. 244, 2013 ABCA 109 at para. 3 (Alta. C.A.). A party can apply to extend her or his time to appeal, by satisfying the four-part test from Cairns v. Cairns (see commentary to rule 12.59). Beck v. Ackmann Sohal , [2013] A.J. No. 244, 2013 ABCA 109 at paras. 3, 4 (Alta. C.A.), citing v. Brar Cairns v. Cairns , [1998] A.J. No. 1003, 1998 ABCA 375 at para. 1 (Alta. C.A.), citing , [1931] A.J. No. 76, 26 Alta. L.R. 69 (Alta. C.A.). However, “...[s]hort time lines in family law matters are important so as to reduce uncertainty to the parties in sensitive situations.” Beck v. Ackmann, [2013] A.J. No. 244, 2013 ABCA 109 at para. 3 (Alta. C.A.).
Standard of Review – The Court of Appeal “cannot retry the case and must not substitute its views for the view of the chambers judge absent reversible error.”  Cheng v. Li, [2015] A.J. No. 1179, 2015 ABCA 322 at para. 29 (Alta. C.A.).

rules.text:
(1) To appeal an order of the Court of Justice to the Court of King’s Bench pursuant to section  Nafie v. Badawy, [2015] A.J. No. 85, 2015 ABCA 36 at para. 122 (Alta. C.A.), leave to appeal refused [2015] S.C.C.A. No. 128 (S.C.C.). The parties had been ordered to apply for case management. Before a case management judge was appointed, the defendant removed a car jointly-owned by him and the plaintiff, leaving her and her children stranded. The plaintiff applied for an order outside of case management regarding the car. The defendant resisted the application on the basis that the plaintiff was required to have the matter addressed by the case management justice. of the (AR Court of Justice Family Law Procedure Regulation 149/2005), a party must (a) file a notice of appeal in Form FL-33 with the Court of King’s Bench court clerk at the judicial centre where the appeal is to be heard, and (b) serve a copy of the filed notice of appeal on the respondent in R. 12.60 [Service on individuals] the Court of King’s Bench.
(2) The notice of appeal must be filed and served (a) within one month following the date on which the order being appealed was pronounced, or (b) if the appellant is able to establish to the Court’s satisfaction the date on which the appellant received notice of the order, within one month following that date.

commentary.text:
Appeals from the Court of Justice to the Court of King’s Bench on family law matters are appeals as of right. Mckerness v. Whitson, [2017] A.J. No. 645, 2017 ABCA 207 at para. 2 (Alta. C.A.). No further appeals of the appeal decision lie as of right. H. (J.W.) v. V. (M.L.), [2018] A.J. No. 1550, 2018 ABQB 1024 at para. 1 (Alta. Q.B.). The one-month time limit is a normal appeal period under Rules. Walker v. Siler, [2017] A.J. No. 1425, 2017 ABQB 810 at para. 26 (Alta. Q.B.).
Pronouncement vs Notice of Order Under Appeal (Rule 12.61(2)) – Where, at the close of a hearing, the decision-maker asks one lawyer to draft an order based on the lawyer’s recommendations and the decision-maker says he will “consider the draft order, and if I think it’s appropriate, to grant it or something like it’”, the relevant date to begin counting the one month time period is the date the appealing party received the filed order because it was unclear what was “pronounced” on the day of the hearing. Johnson v. Jordan, [2013] A.J. No. 2, 2013 ABCA 55 at paras. 3, 7 (Alta. C.A.). At issue in this case was the now repealed rule 12.60(2) which was identical to the wording of 12.61(2).
Appeal Must be Grounded in an Application in the Court Below – If a party wishes to appeal an order, the party must be able to persuade the appeal court that (a) an application was made; (b) an order was granted in relation to such application; and (c) it can identify the appeal record. Absent these hallmarks of an application, there may be no basis for an appeal. F. (A.M.) v. P. (G.H.), [2022] A.J. No. 1418, 2022 ABKB 758 at paras. 34, 37-38 (Alta. K.B.).

rules.title: Appeal memoranda
rules.text:
(1) The appellant must, not later than noon on the 20th day before the date scheduled for the hearing of the appeal, file and serve on the respondent an appeal memorandum setting out (a) the facts in brief, (b) the relief sought by the appellant, (c) the argument and authorities on which the appellant intends to rely in support of the grounds set out in the notice of appeal, and (d) particular references to the evidence to be discussed in relation to the grounds or arguments.
(2) The respondent must, not later than noon on the 10th day before the date scheduled for the hearing of the appeal, file and serve on the appellant an appeal memorandum setting out (a) the respondent’s position on the relief sought by the appellant, (b) the relief, if any, sought by the respondent by way of cross appeal, (c) the argument and authorities on which the respondent intends to rely, and (d) particular references to the evidence to be discussed in relation to the grounds or arguments.

rules.title: When one judge may act in place of or replace another
rules.text:
One judge may act in place of or replace another judge if (a) that other judge dies, (b) that other judge ceases to be a judge, or (c) it is inconvenient, improper, inappropriate or impossible for that other judge to act.

rules.title: Counting months and years
rules.text:
(1) When counting to or from a date in months, time is calculated from the date on which the event or activity occurs in the month to the same-numbered day in a subsequent or previous month, as the case requires.
(2) If the count ends on the 29th, 30th or 31st and there is no same-numbered date in the subsequent or previous month, the count ends on the last day of the subsequent or previous month, as the case requires.
(3) When counting to or from an event or activity in years, time is calculated from the date on which the activity or event occurs in a year to the same-numbered date in a subsequent or previous year, as the case requires.
(4) If the count starts on February 29th and ends in a year that is not a leap year, the count ends on February 28th of that year.

rules.title: Variation of time periods
rules.text:
(1) Unless the Court otherwise orders or a rule otherwise provides, the parties may agree to extend any time period specified in these rules.
(2) The Court may, unless a rule otherwise provides, stay, extend or shorten a time period that is (a) specified in these rules, (b) specified in an order or judgment, or (c) agreed on by the parties.
(3) The order to extend or shorten a time period may be made whether or not the period has expired.

commentary.text:

“Unless a rule otherwise provides” – Rule 13.5(2) applies unless there is an express declaration in the rule in question that provides that rule 13.5 does not apply. Coleman v. Coleman, [2014] A.J. No. 1443, 2014 ABCA 452 at para. 29 (Alta. C.A.). For example, rule 3.26(3) which provides the time for service of a statement of claim, and rule 3.15(2) which provides the time for bringing most originating applications for judicial review, expressly prohibit time from being varied by either the court or the parties.
